title: Chesed — Reader Revelation Vision
excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Chesed — Reader Revelation Vision The Awtsmoos renews each word before the eye can finish one line; Awtsmoos.com should let Torah occupy the foreground while every control waits for its proper time. Evidence already proven Native reader shell is heichelos/post/ awtsmoos.post.html. Critic
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he chesed — reader revelation vision the awtsmoos renews each word before the eye can finish one line; awtsmoos.com should let torah occupy the foreground while every control waits for its proper time. evidence already proven native reader shell is heichelos/post/ awtsmoos.post.html. critical shell css is already extracted into styles/reader controls/critical shell.css and live template.css. the reader root owns a local scope: .post reader localized context. typography, theme, font, preferences, focus mode, auto scroll, command palette, sidebar, comments, and reading intelligence already have modular javascript homes. advanced appearance already uses native , proving progressive disclosure is an established reader language. the current floating controls are typographybtn and commentarybtn; reader settings live in typographydetails. product goal make the text itself feel sovereign. reader controls should be reachable in one gesture, obvious by keyboard, safe on notched mobile screens, and visually quiet when unused. settings should reveal progressively by human intent, never as a permanent dashboard wall. extreme but coherent improvements one local reader z layer vocabulary instead of literal escalation. safe area aware floating controls and settings surfaces. state rich controls with hover capable hover, active, focus visible, pressed/expanded, disabled, and reduced motion behavior. settings hierarchy: daily reading controls first; advanced appearance, automation, and reset separated by semantic disclosure. sidebar and typography surfaces should coordinate rather than overlap each other. reader shell state should be idempotent and testable through small gate/controller classes. no new global selector, global variable, or unrelated page contract.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he gevurah — reader architecture boundaries the awtsmoos has no boundary, yet every useful keli must guard one line; awtsmoos.com lets endless torah remain usable when each control owns one contract by design. candidate architectures a — keep shell css and patch selectors fast but risks preserving hidden layering and ownership debt. b — replace reader controls with a new framework powerful but unnecessary; native modules already model preferences, focus, sidebar, command palette, and scrolling. c — strengthen the existing reader control architecture preferred. preserve public ids and module entrypoints, improve local tokens/styles, and split only files that actually mix responsibilities. d — shadow dom reader shell strong isolation but incompatible with current id based contracts and not justified by present evidence. e — inline per control styles rejected. violates localized modular css and future maintainability. boundaries for the chosen architecture .post reader localized context remains the reader style owner. existing control ids remain stable unless all consumers are proven migrated. preference/storage modules remain separate from dom gates. typography gate owns typography surface lifecycle only. sidebar gate owns sidebar visibility only. popover coordination may close competing surfaces but must not become a god object. css layering uses reader local custom properties, not arbitrary numeric escalation across unrelated surfaces. fixed/mobile reader ui respects safe area insets and never depends on 100vw. any touched source above 120 lines is split by responsibility, not compressed. files to inspect before final write set styles/reader controls/critical shell.css styles/reader controls/live template.css styles/main.css logic/listeners/tiferestypographygate.js logic/listeners/sidebargate.js logic/listeners/popovergate.js logic/initialization/readerpanels.js logic/listeners.js relevant reader tests and browser harnesses

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he tiferes — reader critique before implementation the awtsmoos joins revealed control and concealed depth until both become one design; awtsmoos.com should make the reader powerful without making the reader feel like a machine. thirty safeguards 1. preserve the reading text as the strongest visual hierarchy. 2. preserve every externally consumed reader id. 3. do not duplicate existing preference state. 4. do not duplicate focus mode state. 5. do not duplicate sidebar state. 6. keep typography and sidebar surfaces mutually non obstructive. 7. keep fixed controls inside safe area boundaries. 8. never use component 100vw sizing. 9. replace arbitrary z escalation with reader local tokens. 10. keep all touched reader selectors rooted locally. 11. ensure 320px mobile remains horizontally scroll free. 12. make every actionable control at least touch friendly. 13. use hover styles only on hover capable devices. 14. give controls visible :focus visible treatment. 15. give controls tactile :active treatment without layout shift. 16. preserve expanded/pressed aria truth through javascript gates. 17. preserve escape/outside click dismissal where already expected. 18. restore useful focus after dismissing transient surfaces. 19. do not let settings obscure the active reading line unnecessarily. 20. honor prefers reduced motion. 21. preserve forced colors legibility. 22. keep dynamic custom tincture css confined to its existing runtime slot. 23. do not replace native semantic disclosure with custom div toggles. 24. keep preference persistence independent of surface rendering. 25. keep event listener setup idempotent. 26. split touched executable modules above 120 lines. 27. use tabs only in touched source. 28. re read every touched file from disk after writes. 29. run reader focused tests only after the code tranche is coherent. 30. browser verify narrow mobile and desktop geometry before declaring the reader tranche closed. expected failure modes to hunt fixed controls covering header or text on narrow safe area devices typography panel escaping viewport height competing popovers staying open simultaneously sidebar and typography state disagreeing with aria attributes reduced motion still animating expensive surfaces hidden controls retaining keyboard focus style selectors leaking outside reader root

Phase 1 — source reality 1. Read both reader control CSS files fully. 2. Read main
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he final reader execution plan the awtsmoos renews each chamber before the next control receives its name; awtsmoos.com should let each rewrite reduce accidental complexity while deepening the reader's flame. phase 1 — source reality 1. read both reader control css files fully. 2. read main reader style import topology and line counts. 3. read typography, sidebar, popover, panel initialization, and listener entry modules. 4. trace exact consumers and existing reader tests. 5. record concrete defects only from source evidence. phase 2 — coherent code tranche 6. if shell css contains mixed responsibilities or exceeds the vessel boundary, split it into an import only manifest plus focused local modules. 7. introduce reader local layer/safe area tokens only if the current source lacks a coherent equivalent. 8. rewrite typography/sidebar/popover gates only where actual lifecycle/state debt exists. 9. preserve existing ids and public module exports. 10. keep daily controls primary; fold advanced groups through existing semantic disclosure instead of new permanent chrome. 11. do not modify the html template unless source tracing proves markup changes are necessary. phase 3 — verification and expansion 12. re read every touched file from disk. 13. audit tabs, line counts, selector ownership, numeric z index, viewport hazards, and compressed meaningful logic. 14. run existing preference, utility, command palette, node dom, and reader control tests. 15. run browser/mobile geometry if a reader harness exists; otherwise use the existing local server/chrome path. 16. compare planned versus actual and write the delta. 17. continue to heichelos directory quality, profile/aliases, comments, notifications, composer, and editors after reader verification closes. expected first write set no production file is committed to the write set until phase 1 inspection is complete. the design target is the smallest coherent set that fixes proven reader shell debt without duplicating existing architecture.
